bipartite.kami_theme: A lament that there is no path of escape from the sorrows of this world, even for one who has resolved to renounce it
bipartite.shimo_theme: Even deep in the mountains where the speaker has fled in spiritual resolve, the cry of a deer is heard, proving that sorrow reaches everywhere
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku declares that there is no 'road' (michi) of escape from worldly grief; the shimo-no-ku demonstrates this paradoxically by showing that even the deepest mountain retreat, entered specifically to escape the world through religious withdrawal (omoi iru), still resounds with the deer's mournful cry — the very symbol of autumn sorrow the speaker sought to leave behind. The mountain retreat, expected to be a refuge, instead confirms that grief is inescapable anywhere in the world.

kigo.note: The cry of the deer (shika) in the mountains, especially calling for a mate, is one of the most conventional autumn images in waka, symbolizing loneliness and mournful longing; here it also functions as the sonic proof of the poem's paradox that grief cannot be escaped even in deep mountain seclusion.

kakekotoba.reading_secondary: 夜 (night) — not fully active here, but the base pivot pattern よ is present
kakekotoba.interaction: 世の中 establishes 'the world/society' as the poem's subject of lament; while the classic よ=夜/世 pivot is present in the sound, here the primary and dominant sense is 世 'this life/world' rather than a genuine night-reading, so this is noted with lower confidence as a possible latent pivot rather than a fully operative double meaning.

kakekotoba.reading_secondary: 思ひ入る as a set phrase meaning 'to resolve deeply / to set one's heart upon (religious renunciation)'
kakekotoba.interaction: 思ひ入る functions almost as a compound verb meaning both literally 'to go/press deeply into (the mountains)' and figuratively 'to be deeply resolved/absorbed in thought (toward religious withdrawal)'; the two senses operate simultaneously as the speaker's physical entry into the mountains mirrors his spiritual resolve to escape worldly grief.

source_jp:
世の中よ
道こそなけれ
思ひ入る
山のおくにも
鹿ぞ鳴くなる
